coder_result.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
CRIME_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2017.csv"
ADJ_PATH   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime_df = pd.read_csv(CRIME_PATH)
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Prepare the crime‐rate series, drop the single missing borough
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
crime_series = crime_df.set_index("borough")["crime_rate_value"]
crime_series = crime_series.dropna()            # removes the 1 NaN row

# keep the list of boroughs we will actually analyse
valid_boroughs = set(crime_series.index)
data_points_used = len(valid_boroughs)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build an UNDIRECTED adjacency dictionary {borough: set(neighbours)}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
adjacency = {b: set() for b in valid_boroughs}

for b1, b2 in adj_df[["borough", "neighbor"]].itertuples(index=False):
    # only keep neighbours whose own value is present
    if b1 in valid_boroughs and b2 in valid_boroughs:
        adjacency[b1].add(b2)
        adjacency[b2].add(b1)

# some boroughs might be isolated in the CSV; they already have empty sets

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. For every borough, compute the LOCAL SUM (itself + neighbours)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
local_sums = {}
for b in valid_boroughs:
    local_set = {b} | adjacency[b]                       # union
    # sum only over boroughs that still have non-missing values
    local_value = crime_series.loc[list(local_set)].sum()
    local_sums[b] = local_value

local_sums_series = pd.Series(local_sums)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compute z-scores of the local sums
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mu  = local_sums_series.mean()
std = local_sums_series.std(ddof=1)

z_scores = (local_sums_series - mu) / std

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Identify statistically significant HOT/COLD spots
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
THRESHOLD = 1.96         # 95 % confidence two-tailed

results = []
for b, z in z_scores.items():
    if z > THRESHOLD:
        results.append(f"{b} (HOT, z={z:.3f})")
    elif z < -THRESHOLD:
        results.append(f"{b} (COLD, z={z:.3f})")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Print the required output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
